title: PS-3 Effects of a Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial on feeder cattle performance during a preconditioning program
content:
Abstract
This experiment evaluated the effects of feeding a Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial (DFM) during a 60-day preconditioning program on the performance of feeder cattle. Eighty-four newly-weaned and originated from the same farm (Kentland Farm) were unloaded at the feedlot facility on day -1 and had their body weight recorded after 16-h of water and feed withdrawal on day 0. Calves were ranked by body weight, sex, and age, in a completely randomized design and then allocated to one of 20 drylot pens (4 to 5 calves per pen; 2 heifers and 2 to 3 steers per pen), and assigned to receive 1) a total mixed ration (TMR) plus 165 g of protein-mineral supplement + 3 g of a DFM containing Bacillus licheniformis 809 and B. subtilis 810 (BAC; n = 10; 2.2 × 109 CFU of the mixture/g; Bovacillus, Novonesis, Lyngby, Denmark), or 2) a TMR plus 165 g of protein-mineral supplement without BAC (CON; n = 10). The supplement consisted of 115 g of a commercial mineral mix combined with 50 g of dried distillers’ grains. The supplement was offered as a top dressing and was fully consumed within 30 minutes. Animals were fed daily at 0800 h ad libitum, and refusals were removed and weighed once a week. Samples of feed offered and refusals were collected to calculate dry matter intake (DMI). Final body weight (FBW) was recorded after 60 days following a 16-h feed and water withdrawal. Average daily gain (ADG) was calculated by subtracting the initial BW from the final BW and dividing the result by 60 days. Feed efficiency (FE) was determined by dividing ADG by DMI. Data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS, using pen as the experimental unit. As designed, calf initial BW was similar (P = 0.96) between treatments. A tendency (P = 0.06; Table 2) for greater DMI in calves supplemented with BAC compared with CON calves. Nevertheless, no treatment effects were detected (P ≥ 0.62) for ADG, FE, and FBW between treatments (Table 2). In summary, supplementing recently weaned calves with a Bacillus-based DFM tended to improve dry matter intake, whereas did not impact overall performance during a 60-d preconditioning program.
